semantic_review.log_softmax: The selected original forward/backward Python JITs and wrapper are unchanged. Both originals and the pre-existing integer row-base commutation candidates are copied as complete raw bodies, with sixteen forward and fifteen backward top-level statements. FP32 pointer storage, three unannotated runtime integer dimensions and two constexpr tiles are bound outside each body. Both PID and both arange INT64 casts, the parenthesized three-value M/N/K cast assignment, signed minimum(size-1) clamping before products, masks, negative-infinity/zero padding, all FP32 casts, arithmetic/reductions, exp/log and stores remain exact. Python candidate counterparts explicitly translate already existing Lean candidates and are labeled authored rather than historical sources. The shared frontend accepts only the parenthesis spelling change; the source token is retained. Existing tuple compilation did not capture registers simultaneously, so a later RHS reading an earlier overwritten target is now explicitly rejected instead of accepting wrong Python semantics. Actual independent M/N/K casts are supported; exact program identity, successful integer tuple execution and unsafe/arity rejection tests replay with standard-base audits. No generic parallel-register-capture implementation is claimed. All existing source execution, memory and frame statements are re-proved: strict integer clamped-address equality handles positive dimensions and source masks separately handle every zero-dimension case, without adding dimension conditions. Original and candidate source access safety replays; actual first-three-statement full-state equality uses strict Int multiplication commutation, and identical complete tails compose by run_append, retaining failed-run equality for arbitrary unchanged floating primitives. Authoritative Kernels contain only full quotations, while take/drop decomposition stays in Proofs. All thirty-seven roots preserve independent full-row Real forward/VJP formulas, every retained BM/autotune/warp choice, complete FP grid/schedule equivalence, native graph/reduction/FMA observations, actual Tensor/contiguous input binding, source safety and logical/physical frames. No scalar numerical port, FP identity, input restriction, numerical experiment or hardware-conformance claim is added.
